$comment: Rule DATA for scripts/check-content.mjs. Plan section 15.2 row 3 is explicit: every rule
CODE change lands in one Phase 1 unit, and the per-language typographic assertions from
plan section 13.2 item 2 arrive HERE as data, never as new branches in the script.
Enabling a rule for a locale must therefore be a data change to this file only.
Why this file exists at all: the em-dash rule used to run on every line of every file.
Japanese prose legitimately uses the horizontal bar and the ideographic full stop, Arabic
uses the Arabic comma and semicolon, and Russian typography uses the em dash as its
standard clause separator. A single global blacklist is wrong the moment a second script
exists, so the blacklist became per-script data with per-locale overrides.
`script` values mirror `FontScript` in i18n/locales.config.ts (that file is the roster of
record). A locale absent from `locales` below falls back to `defaultLocale`, i.e. Latin
script with today's exact English behaviour, so adding a locale to the roster can never
silently loosen a guardrail.
The two shapes scripts/check-content.mjs understands. Both are evaluated per line.
Every plan section 13.2 item 2 assertion expresses as one of these:
forbid  - `pattern` (RegExp source) matching a line is a violation.
e.g. de: straight double quotes instead of the low/high pair.
require - a line matching `when` MUST also match `must`, otherwise it is a violation.
e.g. es: a line containing '?' must also contain the opening '¿'.
`flags` defaults to 'u'. An entry with `enabled: false` is never compiled, so an
unfinished assertion is inert; an entry with `enabled: true` and no pattern throws at
load time rather than passing silently.
Data for the affiliate-integrity rule (plan invariant 9, risk R6): under i18n/**, every
outbound scrimba.com URL must route through <AffiliateLink> or carry via=<AFFILIATE_ID>.
The id itself is NOT here; scripts/check-content.mjs reads it from src/constants.ts so it
has exactly one definition.
`allowedProps` is what keeps the rule usable. Most scrimba.com URLs in this repo are JSX
prop values, not anchors: the component either wraps them in <AffiliateLink> itself (so
the param is appended at render time and must NOT be inlined in the MDX) or the value only
reaches JSON-LD, where an affiliate param would be wrong. Without this list a translated
course page would report ~10 false positives and the rule would get switched off.
A prop is still flagged when it sits on a hand-written <a> tag, which is the one shape
that reaches the browser exactly as the translator typed it.
When a new component takes a Scrimba URL prop, add it HERE with its justification.

allowedProps.href: CourseCard, VerdictBox, PricingCTA, WhyScrimba, ComparisonTable render href through <AffiliateLink> (src/components/CourseCard.tsx:91)
allowedProps.url: CourseSchema / ItemListSchema JSON-LD `url`; structured data, never clicked
allowedProps.itemUrl: ReviewSchema JSON-LD itemReviewed.url; structured data, never clicked
allowedProps.sourceUrl: FAQAccordion citation link: a source reference, not a CTA

$comment: Data for the localized-currency price rule. The price patterns themselves are code
(plan section 4 Phase 1), but the comparison connectives are language data and belong
here. A price that sits next to a Scrimba plan across one of these words is a competitor
comparison ('30 € contre Scrimba Pro'), not Scrimba's own price, and must not be flagged.
Add the local 'versus' word when a locale's first pages land.
Per-script punctuation policy. `forbiddenPunctuation` is the blacklist; a locale may
subtract from it via its own `allowedPunctuation`. Only Latin carries the em dash today,
which is what keeps English output byte-identical (plan section 16.1).

latin.$comment: U+2014 EM DASH. The original project style rule; unchanged for en and every Latin-script locale until a translate-<lang> skill argues otherwise in its own `allowedPunctuation`.

cyrillic.$comment: Russian/Ukrainian/Bulgarian тире (U+2014) is the standard clause separator and « » are the standard quotes. Blacklisting them would fail every correct page.

greek.$comment: ano teleia (U+0387) and guillemets are standard Greek punctuation. Plan section 13.2 adds the final-sigma and monosyllable-accent assertions as `rules` on el.

arabic.$comment: Arabic comma, semicolon, question mark, percent sign and tatweel. Plan section 13.2 (ar) also wants ASCII digits for version numbers and durations; that lands as a `forbid` rule on ar.

cjk.$comment: Japanese/Chinese full-width punctuation. U+2015 HORIZONTAL BAR is one Kana keystroke away from U+2014 EM DASH, so no dash is blacklisted here; plan section 13.2 (ja) instead asserts full-width punctuation POSITIVELY as a `rules` entry.

defaultLocale.$comment: Applied to every path outside i18n/<locale>/ (docs, blog, src) and to any locale with no entry below.

$comment: One entry per locale that has a typographic profile. `rules` is intentionally EMPTY or
disabled everywhere today: this commit adds zero locales, and each assertion is authored
with its language's translate-<lang>/SKILL.md (plan section 13.2 item 2), which is where
the linguistic justification lives. The disabled entries below are the checklist of what
that section owes this file, not dead code: fill in `pattern`/`when`/`must` and flip
`enabled` to true. No change to scripts/check-content.mjs is required or permitted.

rules.message: French requires a narrow no-break space (U+202F) before ? ! ; : and inside « »
rules.$comment: Plan section 13.2 (fr). Also forbids straight " " quotes in favour of « ». Pattern must tolerate code spans and URLs, which is why it is not written blind here.

rules.message: German prose uses „ " quotes, not straight double quotes
rules.$comment: Plan section 13.2 (de). The ß/ss Swiss-variant decision belongs in the same entry set once the de skill picks a variant.

rules.message: Spanish question/exclamation sentences require the opening ¿ / ¡
rules.$comment: Plan section 13.2 (es). `when` matches a line ending a question, `must` asserts the opening mark on the same line.

rules.message: Japanese prose uses 、 and 。, never ASCII comma/period, and takes no space around parentheses
rules.$comment: Plan section 13.2 (ja). Must not fire inside code spans, version numbers or URLs, which is the entire difficulty of this rule.

rules.message: Turkish dotted/dotless i casing trap: 'IT' lowercased to 'ıt' is a silent corruption
rules.$comment: Plan section 13.2 (tr). Targets do-not-translate terms whose casing was run through a Turkish-locale toLowerCase.

rules.message: Greek final sigma ς is word-final only; no accent on monosyllables
Arabic pages use ASCII digits for version numbers and durations, to match the code they sit beside
rules.$comment: Plan section 13.2 (ar). Eastern Arabic-Indic digits ٠-٩ in a version number or an hours figure are the violation.
